Yes, head positioning can influence anterior chamber depth in pseudoexfoliation syndrome. Specifically, patients with clinically apparent unilateral pseudoexfoliation may experience a shallower anterior chamber when their head is placed in a prone position.

This occurs because the lens in the affected eye becomes more mobile and causes a shallower anterior chamber, potentially leading to transient pupillary block and other complications. Further study is needed to fully understand this relationship and to determine whether this effect can be mitigated through treatment or management strategies.
